evaluated.name: IntangibleWeightedCheapness
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Book-based cheapness is most informative precisely where accounting most understates capital, i.e., in R&D-intensive firms; among asset-heavy, low-R&D firms, book value is already close to economic capital, so B/M carries less mispricing information.
evaluated.reasoning: The centered cheapness score is amplified by the firm's R&D intensity rank, so high-B/M knowledge firms load strongly positive and low-B/M knowledge firms strongly negative, while tangible-heavy firms are shrunk toward neutral. This is a conditional (slope-modulating) interaction rather than an additive combination of two independent effects.

evaluated.name: ValueWithRisingIntangibleEffort
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MA(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 1), 3))
evaluated.hypothesis: A cheap valuation plus rising intangible investment intensity signals an underpriced firm still reinvesting in future knowledge capital, whereas a cheap valuation plus shrinking R&D intensity signals genuine franchise decay (a value trap).
evaluated.reasoning: Smoothed changes in R&D-to-sales capture whether the intangible capital stock is being sustained, which determines whether the intangible-adjusted book value is forward-looking or a fossil of past spending. The interaction is a state-plus-flow condition: the same measured cheapness carries opposite economic content depending on the direction of intangible effort.

evaluated.name: KnowledgeEffortVsEnterpriseMultiple
evaluated.expression: SUB(RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Put intangible investment and market valuation on the same denominator (sales) and compare them: firms that spend heavily per sales dollar on knowledge and brand while the market capitalizes each sales dollar cheaply have intangible effort that is not embedded in price, and that expectation mismatch reverses in future returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the published capitalize-R&D-into-book construction entirely: no intangible stock is added to equity and no goodwill is stripped, so it is not a re-statement of intangible-adjusted B/M. Instead it is a units-matched wedge between what the firm invests per sales dollar and what the market pays per sales dollar (enterprise value, which sidesteps negative and intangible-padded book equity), and sales-scaling keeps both legs finite and defined for essentially all firms with revenue.

evaluated.name: AmortizationBlindEnterpriseYield
evaluated.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))))), RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms carrying large capitalized intangible balances report earnings depressed by non-cash intangible amortization and are further discounted for impairment fear, so pre-amortization cash-operating cheapness (EBITDA/EV) contains the most mispricing information exactly in that group, while for intangible-light firms EBITDA and earnings say nearly the same thing.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the additive add-back (which was algebraically E/P + R&D/MV) with a slope-modulating structure: the centered cheapness score is scaled by the firm's balance-sheet intangible weight, so intangible-light firms are shrunk toward neutral and cannot be decomposed into two standalone anomaly sums. The mechanism is the acquired-intangible amortization/impairment channel, distinct from the R&D-expensing channel used elsewhere in the set.

evaluated.name: CheapReturnOnKnowledgeCapital

evaluated.hypothesis: Cheapness only pays when the firm earns a high gross return on its full economic capital base, tangible plus accumulated knowledge capital; cheap firms that produce little gross profit per dollar of intangible-augmented capital are value traps whose knowledge stock is economically impaired.
evaluated.reasoning: The productivity leg now divides by ADD(at, 5-year R&D stock) rather than by the intangible stock alone, so it is finite and well-defined for tangible-heavy firms and no longer explodes when intangibles are near zero — the ranks reflect economics, not division artifacts. The valuation leg is plain B/M, not the published intangible-adjusted B/M, and it enters multiplicatively so the intangible term modulates the cheapness slope instead of contributing an independent additive tilt.

evaluated.reasoning: This drops the three-channel stack for one interpretable q-theoretic ratio with no implicit weights: a single asset-side replacement cost measured with intangible economics, priced against whole-firm enterprise value rather than equity. It differs from intangible-adjusted book-to-market in both directions of the adjustment — purchased intangibles are removed as non-reproducible while organic R&D outlays are added at cost — and it is defined for every firm with assets and a market price, keeping coverage at archive levels.

evaluated.hypothesis: The commitment floor identifies firms whose knowledge capital is genuinely funded every year, and it should pay off against whichever cheapness metric is least corrupted by intangible accounting; enterprise cash-operating yield is immune to both book-equity understatement and intangible amortization, so it should pair better with the commitment floor than book-to-market does.

evaluated.name: CheapWithDurableMarginMoat
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: The largest category of unrecorded intangible capital — brand equity, customer switching costs, distribution relationships — is never reported as spending at all, and it reveals itself only as a gross margin the firm can defend year after year; cheap firms with a high floor under their margin therefore own economic capital that no balance sheet or R&D line item captures.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the ensemble-of-two-winners with an intangible proxy from an entirely different observable channel — realized pricing power rather than reported intangible spending — so it cannot be an interpolation between existing alphas. It also repairs the structural weakness common to every R&D leg in the archive: the COALESCE(xrd,0) mass point that ties over half the cross-section at the bottom rank, since gross margin is continuous and defined for essentially all firms with revenue.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashCheapMinusPurchasedKnowledge
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The acquired-intangible penalty is specifically about *buying knowledge instead of building it*: identifiable purchased intangibles — patents, licences, customer lists, developed technology — are knowledge assets a firm chose to acquire at a negotiated premium rather than create, and such purchased knowledge earns lower returns than the internally built kind that never reaches the balance sheet.
evaluated.reasoning: The decomposition evidence points here: total intangibles as the penalty leg gave 4.4% alpha while the goodwill-only component gave only 2.5%, so the identifiable non-goodwill component is the untested piece that the arithmetic implicates as the stronger driver. Establishing that the penalty attaches to purchased *knowledge* rather than to acquisition premia generally would unify the archive's two validated channels into a single organic-versus-acquired knowledge story and dictate how the final generations construct the intangible leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TwoChannelUnrecordedCapitalValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Unrecorded capital comes in two forms that different firms hold: knowledge capital, visible only as sustained R&D spending, and brand/relationship capital, visible only as a defended gross margin. A value screen that reads both should identify understated book value across the whole cross-section, not just among R&D reporters.
evaluated.reasoning: The R&D floor is identically zero for roughly half the market, so for those firms the intangible leg contributes no ranking information at all, while the margin floor is continuous and defined for nearly every firm with revenue — the two legs are informative about disjoint sets of firms, which is precisely the complementarity condition that was absent in the gen-3 dilution case. Both legs individually generate 3.6–4.7% alpha, so if the complementarity argument is right this should exceed the 4.7% ceiling rather than interpolate between them.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrossProfitEVWithKnowledgeFloor
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross profit is the income measure least contaminated by intangible accounting — it sits above R&D, advertising, and intangible amortization in the income statement — so scaling it by enterprise value gives the cleanest cheapness metric for intangible-intensive firms and should pair better with the commitment floor than EBITDA, which is reduced by expensed intangible investment.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has tested the commitment floor against three value legs (adjusted B/M 4.7%, EBITDA/EV 4.4%, plain B/M 3.7%) but never against a numerator that is mechanically immune to intangible expensing, which is the theme's core accounting problem — EBITDA is charged for the very R&D the intangible leg rewards, so the two legs currently work against each other inside the same firm. This resolves an internal inconsistency in the winning family rather than permuting ingredients arbitrarily.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithStableMarginMoat
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If margin durability proxies for unrecorded brand and relationship capital, then what matters is the *invariance* of the margin to competitive and cost shocks, not its level: a firm whose gross margin barely moves for five years has pricing power that no balance sheet records, whereas a high but volatile margin is a commodity cycle.
evaluated.reasoning: This isolates one design choice on a channel that just worked (margin floor, 3.6%, t=3.27) — second moment versus floor level — and it separates the intangible-capital interpretation from a simple high-margin tilt that overlaps published gross-profitability results. The volatility construction is legitimate here precisely because it failed for R&D: gross margin has no zero-imputation mass point, so low volatility cannot be an artifact of non-reporting the way NEG(VOL(xrd)) was.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashCheapMinusRevenueUnbackedIntangibles
evaluated.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Purchased intangibles are only defensible if they support commerce: an intangible balance large relative to the revenue it helps generate is capital paid for a customer base or technology that never delivered volume, and cheap firms carrying no such revenue-unbacked intangibles should outperform.
evaluated.reasoning: Sales replaces gross profit as the deflator, which removes the flagged pathology entirely — revenue is strictly positive for essentially every firm in the sample, so no distressed negative-margin firm can be mislabelled as highly productive and pulled into the long leg. The economic claim remains distinct from the archived intan/at penalty: assets-scaling measures how much of the balance sheet is padding, whereas sales-scaling measures whether the acquired intangible is attached to a functioning business, and the two diverge most for asset-light acquirers.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BuiltVersusBoughtMoatValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUB(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The organic-versus-acquired distinction is the central economic story of this theme — capital built internally is invisible and understates book value, capital bought is recorded at a premium already paid — and it is best measured by comparing demonstrated pricing power against recorded purchased intangibles, since durable margin is evidence that intangible capital exists and works regardless of whether the firm reports R&D.
evaluated.reasoning: The earlier built-minus-bought composition test diluted to 3.2% for a diagnosable reason: its organic half was the R&D floor, which is identically zero for roughly half the cross-section, so the difference collapsed toward the purchased-intangible leg alone for most firms. Replacing that half with margin durability — continuous, full-coverage, and already validated at 3.6% standalone — makes the composition genuinely two-sided for every firm, which is a mechanism repair rather than the asset-turnover leg the critic correctly rejected.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithKnowledgeAccretionYield
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), csho), 1), prcc_f))
evaluated.hypothesis: What a shareholder actually receives from intangible investment is the annual increase in knowledge capital attributable to each share, and the right benchmark for that increase is the share price: a firm adding unrecorded capital worth a large fraction of its stock price each year is accreting value the market is not pricing, and dilution reduces this accretion mechanically rather than as a separate effect.
evaluated.reasoning: Issuance can no longer dominate because csho enters only as the denominator of the per-share knowledge stock, so the leg is a smooth accretion yield rather than the difference between a slow-moving R&D series and a spiky issuance series — this addresses the flagged concern structurally, not by relabelling. Scaling by price makes the leg an intangible analogue of a per-share earnings yield, so both themes are present within the single variable, and non-reporters take the well-defined value zero rather than becoming undefined.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrossProfitValueDualFloors
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The best available cheapness metric for intangible-intensive firms is gross profit to enterprise value, because gross profit is the only income measure booked above intangible expensing; combining it with the two complementary proxies for unrecorded capital — funded knowledge investment and defended pricing power — should give the cleanest possible reading of value that accounting understates.
evaluated.reasoning: This crosses the archive's two independent gen-5 findings: the value-leg upgrade worth roughly +0.5pp (GP/EV over EBITDA/EV against an identical intangible leg) and the dual-floor intangible construction worth roughly +1.4pp over a single floor. Both improvements were established while holding the other component fixed, so the combination is a directed consolidation rather than a blind permutation, and its failure would be as informative as its success about whether the two gains are independent.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IndustryRelativeMarginMoatValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), IND_ADJ(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross margin levels are dictated far more by industry cost structure than R&D intensity is, so a firm's margin floor relative to its own sector — not its absolute level — is the part that reflects firm-specific intangible capital such as brand and switching costs.
evaluated.reasoning: Industry demeaning cut the R&D commitment channel roughly in half (4.4%→2.5%), but the same test has never been run on the moat channel where the prior runs the other way, since raw margins compare software to grocery while raw R&D intensity at least measures a discretionary choice. This is a single-lever change to the archive's best signal and it determines whether the newly discovered moat channel is firm-level mispricing or a sector tilt that later generations should treat differently.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ConjunctiveCheapMoat
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The mispricing genuinely requires both conditions — the firm must be cheap *and* possess defended pricing power — so a conjunctive score should isolate it more sharply than an average that lets extreme cheapness substitute for the absence of a moat.
evaluated.reasoning: Conjunction was tested once and underperformed (2.8% versus 4.4%), but with a diagnosed cause the critic identified: the R&D floor ties roughly half the cross-section at an identical IND_RANK, so MIN was capped at a tie value for a huge block of firms and the short leg was near-arbitrary. The margin floor is continuous with no imputation mass point, which makes this the first valid test of conjunctive combination and a genuine repair rather than a re-run.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CheapWithoutMarginErosion
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUB(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: A cheap firm whose gross margin sits at its own five-year peak still commands the pricing power its intangible capital confers, whereas one trading far below its own peak margin is watching that unrecorded capital depreciate — competitors have copied the product, the brand has faded, or customers have gained bargaining power — and its low price is justified.
evaluated.reasoning: On this channel the level floor worked (+3.6%) and the volatility measure failed (−2.0%), which points to erosion-from-peak as the untested middle concept: it captures deterioration in intangible capital rather than its noisiness, and it is exactly zero for firms currently at their peak so the top of the distribution is well-populated and economically homogeneous. It also gives the batch one signal about the *depreciation* of unrecorded capital, a state variable no archive signal measures.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PurgedBookValueDualFloors
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Book equity should be rebuilt on both sides of the intangible distortion before it is compared to price: add the knowledge capital that expensing removed, and subtract the purchased intangibles that acquisition accounting inserted at a negotiated premium. The resulting reconstructed equity is the economically reproducible capital of the firm, and cheapness measured against it is what the market misprices.
evaluated.reasoning: This folds the fourth validated channel into the accounting definition of the value ratio instead of bolting it on as another rank, which removes the weighting problem entirely — the structure stays two-legged with an unambiguous half weight on value and a quarter on each unrecorded-capital proxy. The placement is mechanically correct rather than arbitrary: intan sits inside ceq, so removing it corrects the numerator of the ratio itself, which is exactly why the padding penalty was worth 4.4% standalone.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BuiltVersusBoughtPerRevenueValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUB(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Measured against the same revenue base, the two forms of intangible capital point in opposite directions: pricing power that a firm has defended year after year is capital it built and never recorded, while intangible assets carried per dollar of sales are capital it bought and did record, at a price already paid. Cheap firms at the built end of that spectrum are where reported book value most understates economics.
evaluated.reasoning: Both halves of the composition leg are now deflated by revenue, so the comparison is between two intangible positions measured on a common commercial base rather than one on assets and one on margin — and the revenue-deflated penalty was the higher-Sharpe version of that channel (0.484 versus 0.455). The value numerator is gross profit because it is the only income line charged for neither R&D nor advertising, which is the correct version of the mechanism the critic rejected: EBITDA is pre-amortisation but still net of the intangible investment the signal rewards.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PurgedValueWithKnowledgeFloor
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: The purge of purchased intangibles and the R&D commitment floor are the two ingredients with the clearest mechanical link to the accounting failure; the gross-margin floor may be adding a generic profitability tilt rather than incremental intangible information.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the second arm of the attribution: against the 7.8% dual-floor version it measures exactly what the margin floor contributes once the value leg is purged, and against the 4.7% unpurged single-floor signal it measures what the purge contributes at fixed intangible structure. Given the critic's observation that gross profit already enters the GP/EV family twice, establishing whether the margin floor is additive or redundant is necessary before the final consolidation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BrandInclusiveReconstructionValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xad, 0), 5))), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If expensed R&D belongs in book equity then expensed advertising does too — brand-building outlays create customer capital with multi-year returns and are written off immediately — so the reconstruction should capitalise both forms of intangible investment, not only the technological one.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's reconstruction has always capitalised R&D only, which understates the equity of consumer-facing firms exactly as expensing understates that of technology firms — and unlike a floor built on xad, a *cumulative* advertising stock added to book equity is meaningful even for firms reporting advertising in only some years. It is a single, economically motivated lever on the best signal, and the coverage cost is nil because non-reporters simply contribute zero brand capital.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PurgedValueWithAllocationChoice
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dvc), at))
evaluated.hypothesis: The intangible channel that matters alongside a corrected value ratio may be management's *choice* between building invisible capital and distributing cash, rather than the level of investment: a cheap firm on corrected book that is directing cash into knowledge and brand instead of dividends is compounding capital the market cannot see.
evaluated.reasoning: The allocation channel produced 3.6% alpha with Sharpe 0.496 but has only ever been paired with EBITDA/EV, never with the corrected book value that has since proven far stronger, so this fills a cell whose economics differ from the floors — it measures a decision, not a stock. It also gives the batch one intangible leg that is not a TS_MIN floor, guarding against the possibility that the archive's success is specific to floor-type constructions.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TangibleBookPurgedDualFloors
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Once unrecorded capital is screened for separately through the commitment and margin floors, capitalising R&D inside the value ratio may be redundant double-counting of the same spending; what the ratio still needs is the removal of purchased intangibles, which no other channel corrects.
evaluated.reasoning: This completes the decomposition of the archive's best signal: with unpurged-capitalised at 6.1% and purged-capitalised at 7.8%, the purged-uncapitalised version identifies whether the gain came from removing intan or from adding R&D — and a strong result here would mean the whole family can be simplified to tangible-book cheapness plus two unrecorded-capital screens. Simplicity matters for the final generations because every extra term in the value leg is another place where the same R&D dollars enter twice with an unexamined weight.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: FastDepreciationKnowledgeValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Knowledge capital depreciates fast — competitors imitate, patents age, platforms are superseded — so a five-year undepreciated accumulation of R&D overstates the surviving capital of firms whose spending peaked years ago; a three-year window implies a much higher depreciation rate and should give a truer reconstructed equity if obsolescence is quick.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not the published ratio stripped of screens but a test of its central free parameter — the assumed survival rate of intangible capital — held against the archive's benchmark structure so the comparison with the 7.8% five-year version isolates exactly that economic quantity. It also fixes the monotonicity objection to a standalone ratio: the reconstruction enters a rank-based composite where a negative numerator simply lands at the bottom rather than creating a sign flip.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: FirmLevelReproducibleCapitalValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The two-sided intangible correction can be applied at the level of the whole firm rather than of the equity claim: what a competitor would have to spend to reproduce the business is tangible assets plus the cumulative organic R&D outlay, excluding purchased intangibles that cannot be reproduced at book cost, and the right price for that base is enterprise value rather than market equity.
evaluated.reasoning: The firm-level version of this correction was tested once as a raw unranked ratio and failed (−0.5% alpha despite fmb 4.42), a pattern the archive has repeatedly shown to come from unbounded linear ratios whose tails are dominated by leverage — embedding it in the validated rank structure with the dual floors held fixed determines whether the earlier failure was the economics or the functional form. It keeps the same two-leg, three-ingredient complexity as the current best signal, so a win is attributable to the equity-versus-firm-level choice rather than to added channels.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: FirmLevelTangibleCapitalValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The redundancy discovered on the equity side should hold on the asset side too: once knowledge commitment is screened separately, adding cumulative R&D to the capital base only re-uses the same information, and the enterprise multiple should be taken on hard, non-purchased assets alone.
evaluated.reasoning: The firm-level formulation delivered the archive's best t-statistic and FMB slope (6.20 and 5.45) but 1.8pp less alpha than the equity-level version, and the single change that lifted the equity version — dropping the R&D add-back — has never been applied to it. This is the most direct route to a signal that is simultaneously large and precise, which is what the multi-metric objective requires.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GoodwillPurgedBookDualFloors
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If the purge works because acquisition premia inflate book equity, then removing goodwill — the pure residual premium — should capture most of the benefit, whereas if identifiable purchased intangibles such as patents and customer lists are equally suspect, the full purge will dominate.
evaluated.reasoning: The equivalent decomposition inside the rank-difference family gave 2.5% for goodwill versus 4.4% for total intangibles, implying the effect is broader than goodwill, but that test used the penalty as a separate ranked leg rather than as a correction inside the value ratio — where the mechanics are different because goodwill is the part of book equity with no separable asset behind it. Establishing which component drives the strongest signal in the archive is essential before the final generation fixes a specification.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TotalIntangibleSpendFloorValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Committed intangible investment includes brand building as well as research, so the commitment floor should be measured on total intangible spending; a consumer firm that has advertised heavily every year for five years is as committed to unrecorded capital as a technology firm that has researched every year.
evaluated.reasoning: Advertising was tested inside the value reconstruction (7.5% versus 8.3% for the pure purge) but never inside the screen, which is the place where the redundancy logic says intangible spending information belongs now that the value leg has been stripped of it. The critic's caveat about xad disclosure is real and cuts the right way here: a firm that consistently *reports* material advertising is revealing a deliberate, sustained brand programme, which is exactly what a commitment floor should capture.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AllocationScreenReplacesCommitmentFloor
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dvc), at), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What identifies hidden capital may be management's revealed preference for building it over distributing cash, rather than the historical floor of spending; the allocation choice is forward-looking where the floor is backward-looking, and it should substitute for the commitment floor alongside the margin screen.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a substitution test rather than another stacked channel: the allocation flow paired with corrected book value produced 6.2% alpha on its own, and if it can replace the R&D floor without loss it means the archive's dependence on TS_MIN constructions is incidental rather than essential. That distinction matters for the final generation, because a floor is a slow, sticky variable while an allocation ratio updates every year and turns the portfolio over faster.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OperatingCashYieldDualFloors
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oancf, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating cash flow is the one income measure that neither capitalises nor amortises anything — it charges intangible investment in full when paid and is immune to the D&A of purchased intangibles — so as a cheapness metric it needs no reconstruction at all, and paired with the two unrecorded-capital screens it tests whether the elaborate balance-sheet correction can be bypassed entirely.
evaluated.reasoning: Every value leg in the archive has been either a book reconstruction or an accrual-based income measure (EBITDA, gross profit, earnings); realised cash flow is the untested alternative and it addresses the theme's problem from the opposite direction — instead of repairing a distorted balance sheet, it uses the statement that intangible accounting cannot distort. If it approaches 8% alpha with a strong FMB slope, the final generation should prefer it on robustness grounds, since it requires no assumption about intangible depreciation rates or purge definitions.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: HiddenCapitalPerHardDollarValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The screen should measure the *magnitude of the accounting error*, not the persistence of spending: cumulative knowledge outlay per dollar of hard recorded capital states directly how much of a firm's economic capital is missing from its balance sheet, so a hard-book value ratio is most understated precisely for firms where that ratio is large.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the mechanism of the commitment screen rather than its lookback: a five-year minimum intensity is a durability test that answers "has this firm always invested," whereas hidden capital per hard dollar answers "how wrong is the reported book," which is the quantity the theme's economics actually implicates and which no archive signal has measured. The deflator is deliberately hard assets rather than total assets, so purchased intangibles cannot dilute the measured understatement, and the whole leg stays bounded below at zero with non-reporters correctly placed at the bottom rather than tied arbitrarily.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OperatingMarginMoatHardValue
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(ebitda, sale), 5)))

considered.hypothesis: When the two leading value metrics for intangible-intensive firms disagree, the cash-based one is right: a firm that ranks cheap on knowledge-capitalized book equity but expensive on enterprise cash yield is cheap only because its reconstructed book is large relative to a business generating no cash, and it should underperform the reverse case.
considered.reasoning: Unlike the flagged wedge, this is not a monotone transform of R&D-to-market — the two legs use different numerators (reconstructed equity versus cash operating profit) and different denominators (market equity versus enterprise value), so their rank difference is driven by cash generation conditional on reconstructed asset value, not by R&D capital alone. It also directly adjudicates the archive's central tension, since the EV cash-yield leg has produced the strongest slopes and Sharpes while book-based reconstruction legs have been the weaker partner in every composite.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashCheapMinusGoodwillPremium
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The purchased-intangible penalty is specifically a goodwill penalty: goodwill is the residual premium paid above identifiable assets, so it measures accumulated overpayment, whereas identifiable purchased intangibles such as patents and customer lists are genuine productive assets that should not be penalized in a value screen.
considered.reasoning: This decomposes the archive's best signal (EV cash yield minus intan/at, alpha 4.4%, Sharpe 0.455) into its economically distinct components and is in no way collinear with the R&D commitment floor, addressing the redundancy objection to the previous proposal. If the goodwill-only version matches or beats the total-intangible version, the mechanism is overpayment in acquisitions rather than balance-sheet padding generally, which changes how every subsequent signal should treat identifiable intangibles.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BookCheapMinusAcquiredIntangibles
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The purchased-intangible penalty should be strongest where the padding actually distorts the valuation ratio itself: intan sits inside book equity, so a firm can rank cheap on reconstructed book-to-market precisely because acquisition accounting inflated its book, and removing those firms should improve the book-based value leg more than it improves a cash-flow leg that never touches book equity.
considered.reasoning: This fills the one empty cell of the valuation-leg × intangible-leg grid (book cheapness paired with the acquired-intangible penalty), and unlike the EV version it has a mechanical rationale for why the two legs interact rather than merely add — the penalized quantity is a component of the value ratio's numerator. If it beats the 4.4% EV version, subsequent work should build the acquired-intangible screen onto book-based rather than cash-based value.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SectorKnowledgeIntensityValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUB(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), IND_ADJ(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: The mispricing of unrecorded intangible capital operates at the sector level, not the firm level: whole knowledge-intensive industries have systematically understated book values that factor models built on reported accounting cannot capture, so cheapness pays most in high-R&D sectors regardless of a firm's rank within its own sector.
considered.reasoning: Subtracting the industry-demeaned floor from the raw floor isolates exactly the industry-mean component, which is the piece implicated by gen-3's finding that demeaning cut the alpha from 4.4% to 2.5% — this converts that inference into a direct test. It matters for interpretation: if the between-industry component alone reproduces most of the alpha, the mechanism is sector-level accounting distortion rather than firm-level commitment, and the FF5 factors' reliance on reported book equity is the reason it survives risk adjustment.

considered.name: CheapWithKnowledgeOverBrickInvestment
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUB(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(DELTA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 1), LAG(at, 1)), 3)), IND_RANK(GROWTH(at, 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Among cheap firms, what matters is the *composition* of investment: management directing incremental capital into knowledge that never appears on the balance sheet, rather than into balance-sheet expansion, is building value the market cannot observe, whereas the cheap firm growing total assets is empire-building in plain sight.
considered.reasoning: This is a new channel — the intangible-versus-tangible investment mix — rather than another measure of intangible investment level, and it interacts with valuation because a low multiple means the market is pricing neither form of growth. Both halves of the mix leg are industry percentiles, so neither can dominate the other by scale, which was the magnitude flaw that sank the earlier net-composition attempt.

considered.name: PlainValueWithKnowledgeCommitment
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Capitalizing R&D into book equity may add nothing once a separate R&D commitment leg is present, because the reconstructed book and the commitment measure are driven by the same spending; if plain book-to-market plus the commitment floor matches the intangible-adjusted version, the entire capitalization adjustment is redundant double-counting rather than a correction.
considered.reasoning: Every strong archive signal capitalizes R&D into the value leg *and* adds an R&D-based intangible leg, which means R&D enters twice with unexamined weight — this ablation determines whether the accounting reconstruction or the commitment screen is doing the work. A null difference would be a substantive finding that redirects remaining generations toward better intangible legs rather than better book reconstructions.

considered.name: CheapWithDurableMarginMoat
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
considered.hypothesis: The largest category of unrecorded intangible capital — brand equity, customer switching costs, distribution relationships — is never reported as spending at all, and it reveals itself only as a gross margin the firm can defend year after year; cheap firms with a high floor under their margin therefore own economic capital that no balance sheet or R&D line item captures.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the ensemble-of-two-winners with an intangible proxy from an entirely different observable channel — realized pricing power rather than reported intangible spending — so it cannot be an interpolation between existing alphas. It also repairs the structural weakness common to every R&D leg in the archive: the COALESCE(xrd,0) mass point that ties over half the cross-section at the bottom rank, since gross margin is continuous and defined for essentially all firms with revenue.

considered.name: CashCheapMinusPurchasedKnowledge
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: The acquired-intangible penalty is specifically about *buying knowledge instead of building it*: identifiable purchased intangibles — patents, licences, customer lists, developed technology — are knowledge assets a firm chose to acquire at a negotiated premium rather than create, and such purchased knowledge earns lower returns than the internally built kind that never reaches the balance sheet.
considered.reasoning: The decomposition evidence points here: total intangibles as the penalty leg gave 4.4% alpha while the goodwill-only component gave only 2.5%, so the identifiable non-goodwill component is the untested piece that the arithmetic implicates as the stronger driver. Establishing that the penalty attaches to purchased *knowledge* rather than to acquisition premia generally would unify the archive's two validated channels into a single organic-versus-acquired knowledge story and dictate how the final generations construct the intangible leg.

considered.name: TwoChannelUnrecordedCapitalValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Unrecorded capital comes in two forms that different firms hold: knowledge capital, visible only as sustained R&D spending, and brand/relationship capital, visible only as a defended gross margin. A value screen that reads both should identify understated book value across the whole cross-section, not just among R&D reporters.

Both legs individually generate 3.6–4.7% alpha, so if the complementarity argument is right this should exceed the 4.7% ceiling rather than interpolate between them.

considered.name: GrossProfitEVWithKnowledgeFloor
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Gross profit is the income measure least contaminated by intangible accounting — it sits above R&D, advertising, and intangible amortization in the income statement — so scaling it by enterprise value gives the cleanest cheapness metric for intangible-intensive firms and should pair better with the commitment floor than EBITDA, which is reduced by expensed intangible investment.

This resolves an internal inconsistency in the winning family rather than permuting ingredients arbitrarily.

considered.name: CheapWithStableMarginMoat
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), NEG(VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: If margin durability proxies for unrecorded brand and relationship capital, then what matters is the *invariance* of the margin to competitive and cost shocks, not its level: a firm whose gross margin barely moves for five years has pricing power that no balance sheet records, whereas a high but volatile margin is a commodity cycle.

The volatility construction is legitimate here precisely because it failed for R&D: gross margin has no zero-imputation mass point, so low volatility cannot be an artifact of non-reporting the way NEG(VOL(xrd)) was.

considered.name: CashCheapMinusRevenueUnbackedIntangibles
considered.expression: SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), sale)))
considered.hypothesis: Purchased intangibles are only defensible if they support commerce: an intangible balance large relative to the revenue it helps generate is capital paid for a customer base or technology that never delivered volume, and cheap firms carrying no such revenue-unbacked intangibles should outperform.

The economic claim remains distinct from the archived intan/at penalty: assets-scaling measures how much of the balance sheet is padding, whereas sales-scaling measures whether the acquired intangible is attached to a functioning business, and the two diverge most for asset-light acquirers.

considered.name: BuiltVersusBoughtMoatValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUB(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at))))
considered.hypothesis: The organic-versus-acquired distinction is the central economic story of this theme — capital built internally is invisible and understates book value, capital bought is recorded at a premium already paid — and it is best measured by comparing demonstrated pricing power against recorded purchased intangibles, since durable margin is evidence that intangible capital exists and works regardless of whether the firm reports R&D.
considered.reasoning: The earlier built-minus-bought composition test diluted to 3.2% for a diagnosable reason: its organic half was the R&D floor, which is identically zero for roughly half the cross-section, so the difference collapsed toward the purchased-intangible leg alone for most firms. Replacing that half with margin durability — continuous, full-coverage, and already validated at 3.6% standalone — makes the composition genuinely two-sided for every firm, which is a mechanism repair rather than the asset-turnover leg the critic correctly rejected.

considered.name: CheapWithKnowledgeAccretionYield
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), csho), 1), prcc_f))
considered.hypothesis: What a shareholder actually receives from intangible investment is the annual increase in knowledge capital attributable to each share, and the right benchmark for that increase is the share price: a firm adding unrecorded capital worth a large fraction of its stock price each year is accreting value the market is not pricing, and dilution reduces this accretion mechanically rather than as a separate effect.
considered.reasoning: Issuance can no longer dominate because csho enters only as the denominator of the per-share knowledge stock, so the leg is a smooth accretion yield rather than the difference between a slow-moving R&D series and a spiky issuance series — this addresses the flagged concern structurally, not by relabelling. Scaling by price makes the leg an intangible analogue of a per-share earnings yield, so both themes are present within the single variable, and non-reporters take the well-defined value zero rather than becoming undefined.

considered.name: GrossProfitValueDualFloors
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The best available cheapness metric for intangible-intensive firms is gross profit to enterprise value, because gross profit is the only income measure booked above intangible expensing; combining it with the two complementary proxies for unrecorded capital — funded knowledge investment and defended pricing power — should give the cleanest possible reading of value that accounting understates.
considered.reasoning: This crosses the archive's two independent gen-5 findings: the value-leg upgrade worth roughly +0.5pp (GP/EV over EBITDA/EV against an identical intangible leg) and the dual-floor intangible construction worth roughly +1.4pp over a single floor. Both improvements were established while holding the other component fixed, so the combination is a directed consolidation rather than a blind permutation, and its failure would be as informative as its success about whether the two gains are independent.

considered.name: IndustryRelativeMarginMoatValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), IND_ADJ(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Gross margin levels are dictated far more by industry cost structure than R&D intensity is, so a firm's margin floor relative to its own sector — not its absolute level — is the part that reflects firm-specific intangible capital such as brand and switching costs.
considered.reasoning: Industry demeaning cut the R&D commitment channel roughly in half (4.4%→2.5%), but the same test has never been run on the moat channel where the prior runs the other way, since raw margins compare software to grocery while raw R&D intensity at least measures a discretionary choice. This is a single-lever change to the archive's best signal and it determines whether the newly discovered moat channel is firm-level mispricing or a sector tilt that later generations should treat differently.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ConjunctiveCheapMoat
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The mispricing genuinely requires both conditions — the firm must be cheap *and* possess defended pricing power — so a conjunctive score should isolate it more sharply than an average that lets extreme cheapness substitute for the absence of a moat.
considered.reasoning: Conjunction was tested once and underperformed (2.8% versus 4.4%), but with a diagnosed cause the critic identified: the R&D floor ties roughly half the cross-section at an identical IND_RANK, so MIN was capped at a tie value for a huge block of firms and the short leg was near-arbitrary. The margin floor is continuous with no imputation mass point, which makes this the first valid test of conjunctive combination and a genuine repair rather than a re-run.

considered.name: CheapWithoutMarginErosion
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(ebitda, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUB(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: A cheap firm whose gross margin sits at its own five-year peak still commands the pricing power its intangible capital confers, whereas one trading far below its own peak margin is watching that unrecorded capital depreciate — competitors have copied the product, the brand has faded, or customers have gained bargaining power — and its low price is justified.
considered.reasoning: On this channel the level floor worked (+3.6%) and the volatility measure failed (−2.0%), which points to erosion-from-peak as the untested middle concept: it captures deterioration in intangible capital rather than its noisiness, and it is exactly zero for firms currently at their peak so the top of the distribution is well-populated and economically homogeneous. It also gives the batch one signal about the *depreciation* of unrecorded capital, a state variable no archive signal measures.

considered.name: PurgedBookValueDualFloors
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Book equity should be rebuilt on both sides of the intangible distortion before it is compared to price: add the knowledge capital that expensing removed, and subtract the purchased intangibles that acquisition accounting inserted at a negotiated premium. The resulting reconstructed equity is the economically reproducible capital of the firm, and cheapness measured against it is what the market misprices.
considered.reasoning: This folds the fourth validated channel into the accounting definition of the value ratio instead of bolting it on as another rank, which removes the weighting problem entirely — the structure stays two-legged with an unambiguous half weight on value and a quarter on each unrecorded-capital proxy. The placement is mechanically correct rather than arbitrary: intan sits inside ceq, so removing it corrects the numerator of the ratio itself, which is exactly why the padding penalty was worth 4.4% standalone.

considered.name: BuiltVersusBoughtPerRevenueValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUB(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: Measured against the same revenue base, the two forms of intangible capital point in opposite directions: pricing power that a firm has defended year after year is capital it built and never recorded, while intangible assets carried per dollar of sales are capital it bought and did record, at a price already paid. Cheap firms at the built end of that spectrum are where reported book value most understates economics.
considered.reasoning: Both halves of the composition leg are now deflated by revenue, so the comparison is between two intangible positions measured on a common commercial base rather than one on assets and one on margin — and the revenue-deflated penalty was the higher-Sharpe version of that channel (0.484 versus 0.455). The value numerator is gross profit because it is the only income line charged for neither R&D nor advertising, which is the correct version of the mechanism the critic rejected: EBITDA is pre-amortisation but still net of the intangible investment the signal rewards.

considered.name: PurgedValueWithKnowledgeFloor
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5))
considered.hypothesis: The purge of purchased intangibles and the R&D commitment floor are the two ingredients with the clearest mechanical link to the accounting failure; the gross-margin floor may be adding a generic profitability tilt rather than incremental intangible information.
considered.reasoning: This is the second arm of the attribution: against the 7.8% dual-floor version it measures exactly what the margin floor contributes once the value leg is purged, and against the 4.7% unpurged single-floor signal it measures what the purge contributes at fixed intangible structure. Given the critic's observation that gross profit already enters the GP/EV family twice, establishing whether the margin floor is additive or redundant is necessary before the final consolidation.

considered.name: BrandInclusiveReconstructionValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xad, 0), 5))), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: If expensed R&D belongs in book equity then expensed advertising does too — brand-building outlays create customer capital with multi-year returns and are written off immediately — so the reconstruction should capitalise both forms of intangible investment, not only the technological one.

It is a single, economically motivated lever on the best signal, and the coverage cost is nil because non-reporters simply contribute zero brand capital.

considered.name: PurgedValueWithAllocationChoice
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dvc), at))
considered.hypothesis: The intangible channel that matters alongside a corrected value ratio may be management's *choice* between building invisible capital and distributing cash, rather than the level of investment: a cheap firm on corrected book that is directing cash into knowledge and brand instead of dividends is compounding capital the market cannot see.
considered.reasoning: The allocation channel produced 3.6% alpha with Sharpe 0.496 but has only ever been paired with EBITDA/EV, never with the corrected book value that has since proven far stronger, so this fills a cell whose economics differ from the floors — it measures a decision, not a stock. It also gives the batch one intangible leg that is not a TS_MIN floor, guarding against the possibility that the archive's success is specific to floor-type constructions.

considered.hypothesis: Once unrecorded capital is screened for separately through the commitment and margin floors, capitalising R&D inside the value ratio may be redundant double-counting of the same spending; what the ratio still needs is the removal of purchased intangibles, which no other channel corrects.

considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Knowledge capital depreciates fast — competitors imitate, patents age, platforms are superseded — so a five-year undepreciated accumulation of R&D overstates the surviving capital of firms whose spending peaked years ago; a three-year window implies a much higher depreciation rate and should give a truer reconstructed equity if obsolescence is quick.

considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(intan, 0)), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))

considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The redundancy discovered on the equity side should hold on the asset side too: once knowledge commitment is screened separately, adding cumulative R&D to the capital base only re-uses the same information, and the enterprise multiple should be taken on hard, non-purchased assets alone.

considered.name: GoodwillPurgedBookDualFloors
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: If the purge works because acquisition premia inflate book equity, then removing goodwill — the pure residual premium — should capture most of the benefit, whereas if identifiable purchased intangibles such as patents and customer lists are equally suspect, the full purge will dominate.
considered.reasoning: The equivalent decomposition inside the rank-difference family gave 2.5% for goodwill versus 4.4% for total intangibles, implying the effect is broader than goodwill, but that test used the penalty as a separate ranked leg rather than as a correction inside the value ratio — where the mechanics are different because goodwill is the part of book equity with no separable asset behind it. Establishing which component drives the strongest signal in the archive is essential before the final generation fixes a specification.

considered.name: TotalIntangibleSpendFloorValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Committed intangible investment includes brand building as well as research, so the commitment floor should be measured on total intangible spending; a consumer firm that has advertised heavily every year for five years is as committed to unrecorded capital as a technology firm that has researched every year.
considered.reasoning: Advertising was tested inside the value reconstruction (7.5% versus 8.3% for the pure purge) but never inside the screen, which is the place where the redundancy logic says intangible spending information belongs now that the value leg has been stripped of it. The critic's caveat about xad disclosure is real and cuts the right way here: a firm that consistently *reports* material advertising is revealing a deliberate, sustained brand programme, which is exactly what a commitment floor should capture.

considered.name: AllocationScreenReplacesCommitmentFloor
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), dvc), at), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: What identifies hidden capital may be management's revealed preference for building it over distributing cash, rather than the historical floor of spending; the allocation choice is forward-looking where the floor is backward-looking, and it should substitute for the commitment floor alongside the margin screen.
considered.reasoning: This is a substitution test rather than another stacked channel: the allocation flow paired with corrected book value produced 6.2% alpha on its own, and if it can replace the R&D floor without loss it means the archive's dependence on TS_MIN constructions is incidental rather than essential. That distinction matters for the final generation, because a floor is a slow, sticky variable while an allocation ratio updates every year and turns the portfolio over faster.

considered.name: OperatingCashYieldDualFloors
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oancf, ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Operating cash flow is the one income measure that neither capitalises nor amortises anything — it charges intangible investment in full when paid and is immune to the D&A of purchased intangibles — so as a cheapness metric it needs no reconstruction at all, and paired with the two unrecorded-capital screens it tests whether the elaborate balance-sheet correction can be bypassed entirely.
considered.reasoning: Every value leg in the archive has been either a book reconstruction or an accrual-based income measure (EBITDA, gross profit, earnings); realised cash flow is the untested alternative and it addresses the theme's problem from the opposite direction — instead of repairing a distorted balance sheet, it uses the statement that intangible accounting cannot distort. If it approaches 8% alpha with a strong FMB slope, the final generation should prefer it on robustness grounds, since it requires no assumption about intangible depreciation rates or purge definitions.

considered.name: HiddenCapitalPerHardDollarValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The screen should measure the *magnitude of the accounting error*, not the persistence of spending: cumulative knowledge outlay per dollar of hard recorded capital states directly how much of a firm's economic capital is missing from its balance sheet, so a hard-book value ratio is most understated precisely for firms where that ratio is large.
considered.reasoning: This changes the mechanism of the commitment screen rather than its lookback: a five-year minimum intensity is a durability test that answers "has this firm always invested," whereas hidden capital per hard dollar answers "how wrong is the reported book," which is the quantity the theme's economics actually implicates and which no archive signal has measured. The deflator is deliberately hard assets rather than total assets, so purchased intangibles cannot dilute the measured understatement, and the whole leg stays bounded below at zero with non-reporters correctly placed at the bottom rather than tied arbitrarily.

considered.name: OperatingMarginMoatHardValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(ebitda, sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Gross margin flatters intangible-intensive firms because the spending that sustains their pricing power sits below the gross line; a floor on operating margin is a stricter test of whether unrecorded capital actually earns its keep after the overhead required to maintain it.
considered.reasoning: The moat screen has only ever been built from gross margin, yet the archive's own logic says gross profit ignores exactly the intangible spending that the companion screen rewards — measuring durability after those costs asks whether the franchise is self-sustaining rather than merely high-margin. This is a change in the economic content of the screen, not its window, and it should also reduce the mechanical overlap between the two screens noted by the critic.

considered.name: BroadHiddenCapitalMagnitudeValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xad, 0), 5)), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The screen that states the accounting error directly — cumulative intangible outlay per dollar of hard recorded capital — should count brand building as well as research, because both create capital that the balance sheet omits and both therefore contribute to the understatement of book value.
considered.reasoning: Two independent gen-8 results point here: the magnitude screen delivered 8.2% alpha as a substitute for the persistence floor, and broadening the persistence floor from R&D to total intangible spending added roughly half a point — this applies the validated broadening to the validated magnitude construction, a combination no signal has tested. Because it measures an accumulated stock rather than a worst-year minimum, sparse advertising disclosure is less damaging here: any reported advertising years still add to the stock instead of resetting a floor to zero.

considered.name: FirmLevelHardCapitalBroadScreens
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0)), ADD(SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che), ADD(dltt, dlc))), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Pricing hard, non-purchased capital against enterprise value rather than market equity removes the leverage and cash noise from the valuation ratio, which is why that formulation produces the archive's most reliable cross-sectional slope; combined with the broadened commitment screen it should deliver both a large and a precisely estimated abnormal return.
considered.reasoning: The enterprise-level hard-capital leg carries the best FMB t-statistic in the archive (6.25) but 3.8pp less alpha than its equity-level counterpart, and the screen upgrade that raised the equity version from 8.3% to 8.8% has never been applied to it — this is the direct test of whether the two improvements are additive across formulations. Given the objective's explicit refusal to trade magnitude against precision, this is the batch's best candidate for a signal that is strong on both axes simultaneously.

considered.name: HardAssetDeflatedCommitmentValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Commitment to unrecorded capital should be measured against the recorded capital that is actually real: deflating intangible spending by total assets understates the commitment of acquisition-padded firms and overstates nothing, so purging purchased intangibles from the screen's denominator makes the intensity comparable across firms with very different acquisition histories.
considered.reasoning: This keeps assets as the deflator — the archive established at generation 1 that a sales deflator manufactures fake intensity when revenue collapses — and changes only which assets count, applying the same purge logic that lifted the value leg from 6.1% to 8.3% to the screen where it has never been applied. Hard assets are strictly positive for essentially every firm, so the ranking stays monotone and coverage is unaffected.

considered.name: DurableProfitPerHardDollarValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Profit that recorded hard capital cannot explain must come from capital the balance sheet omits, and the inference is only credible if it persists: a five-year floor under gross profit per dollar of hard assets identifies firms that have earned unexplained profits in every year, which is evidence of durable unrecorded capital rather than a temporary boom.
considered.reasoning:
Restoring the TS_MIN construction is the substantive fix: a static level would be gross-profits-to-assets with intangibles netted out, whereas the worst-year floor is a durability statement of the kind that has consistently outperformed static levels in this archive (margin floor +3.6% standalone versus margin volatility −2.0% and margin erosion −1.5%). It substitutes for the margin floor rather than stacking on it, so the test isolates whether hidden capital is better inferred from unexplained profit per unit of recorded capital than from pricing power alone.

considered.name: ExCashHardCapitalValue
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ceq, COALESCE(intan, 0)), che), SUB(MUL(prcc_f, csho), che)), SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at), 5), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Cash is carried at par on the balance sheet and priced at par in the market, so it appears identically in both sides of a book-to-market ratio and simply dilutes the comparison; removing it from both numerator and denominator prices the firm's *operating* hard capital against the market's valuation of that operating business, which is what mispricing attaches to.
considered.reasoning: This avoids the double-counting the critic identified — cash is netted exactly once from each side rather than debt being subtracted from an already net figure — and it targets the archive's one unresolved tension, since the enterprise formulation's superior FMB slope (6.25 versus 4.18) plausibly comes precisely from removing cash and debt noise from the valuation ratio. Intangible-intensive firms hold unusually large cash balances, so this correction bites hardest exactly where the theme says conventional ratios are noisiest.
