critic_notes.rationale: This is a near-verbatim rediscovery of the published intangible-adjusted book-to-market ("intangible value") measure — capitalized R&D added to book equity with goodwill stripped out — so it offers essentially no incremental information beyond an already-documented anomaly.

The conditional construction is internally consistent (centered B/M score scaled by a non-negative R&D-intensity rank shrinks tangible firms toward neutral rather than flipping them), but the COALESCE(xrd,0) mass point means a large majority of firms tie at the bottom rank and have their valuation information mechanically zeroed out, so coverage-effective breadth and portfolio stability need close scrutiny.

Algebraically this is just E/P plus R&D-to-market-cap plus advertising-to-market-cap, i.e., a raw sum of two separately published anomalies (earnings yield and Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis R&D/MV), which makes it a rediscovery rather than a genuine interaction.

The intangible-turnover conditioning leg is a defensible value-trap screen, but the denominator ADD(intan, 5y R&D) is zero or near-zero for the large set of tangible-heavy firms, producing undefined or explosive ratios whose ranks will dominate the composite for reasons unrelated to the stated economics, and the first leg is itself the known intangible-value anomaly.

The hypothesis is explicitly conditional ("cheapness is more understated when intangibles are organic") but the expression is an additive SUMRANK that simply bolts an R&D-intensity tilt onto plain B/M without modulating the cheapness slope, and the organic-share ratio is 0/0 undefined for the many firms with neither R&D nor recorded intangibles.

The state-plus-flow framing is the most genuinely novel of the set and the expected sign is consistent with the abnormal-R&D-increase literature, but it is still additive rather than conditional and ΔR&D/sales rises mechanically when sales collapse, which can load the long leg with distressed firms — the exact opposite of the intended non-value-trap screen.

This is the archived KnowledgeEffortVsEnterpriseMultiple with two parameter-level substitutions (pooled→industry ranks, 1-year flow→5-year sum) and no new economic channel, so it is a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal rather than a substantively different test.

The change addresses a genuine mechanical defect in the archived signal — R&D/sales rising because sales collapse — by deflating the incremental R&D dollar with predetermined lagged assets, which is an economically motivated repair rather than a relabeling, and the expression matches the stated hypothesis.

The COALESCE(xrd,0) imputation makes VOL identically zero for firms that never report R&D, so NEG(VOL) awards them the maximum stability score and the long leg fills with cheap non-innovators — the exact value traps the hypothesis claims to exclude.

Internally consistent and coherently motivated by the gen-0 sign evidence, but it is close to an additive stack of two documented effects (EBITDA/EV value and the goodwill/acquired-intangible underperformance anomaly), and the inference that a multiplicative interaction's negative alpha implies a negative standalone intan/at loading is loose.

Replacing the failed productivity level with a five-year trend is a defensible change in economic content and the sign logic is consistent, though the profitability-trend leg partly rediscovers the published fundamental-trend/profitability-change anomaly and 5-point annual trends are noisy.

This is a kitchen-sink stack of three channels already tested in the archive, with arbitrary implicit weights from the nested SUMRANK (1/2 on cheapness, 1/4 each on the intangible legs), so any result would be uninterpretable and unattributable to a specific mechanism.

This pairs exactly the same two economic legs as the already-evaluated OrganicIntangibleValueTilt (reconstructed book-to-market and net organic-minus-purchased intangibles) and changes only the combination operator from multiplicative to additive, making it a functional-form re-test rather than a new mechanism.

A clean one-variable ablation (swapping book-equity cheapness for EV cash yield while holding the validated R&D commitment floor fixed) that is internally consistent and diagnostically useful, though it is an incremental recombination of two archive legs rather than a new economic channel.

The stock-versus-flow distinction on the acquired-intangible side is a genuine and testable mechanism refinement with correct sign logic, though the goodwill-growth leg overlaps materially with the published asset-growth and post-acquisition underperformance anomalies and should be interpreted with that in mind.

The numerator is essentially R&D-capital-to-market (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis) plus net-cash-to-price minus debt-to-price, i.e. a raw linear stack of three separately published anomalies whose leverage term also predicts *low* returns for high-leverage firms, contradicting the leverage-premium evidence and leaving the composite's sign attribution untestable.

The expression is a symmetric additive rank sum, so it does not "isolate the short leg" as claimed and is not conditional as labelled; economically it is close to the sign-flipped CashCheapMinusAcquiredIntangibles with sales substituted for EBITDA and industry demeaning dropped.

The intangible-investment-versus-payout allocation mix is a genuinely new channel in this archive and the sign logic is coherent, but the leg conflates the R&D/advertising anomaly with a dividend-nonpayer tilt (and xad is near-empty for most firms), so any result will be hard to attribute.

The "identical units" argument fails on magnitude rather than units — TS_MIN(xrd/at) is typically 0–0.05 while intan/at routinely runs 0.1–0.6, so the net leg is arithmetically dominated by −intan/at and the signal collapses into a raw-scaled restatement of the archived CashCheapMinusAcquiredIntangibles rather than a genuine test of a combined organic-minus-acquired position.

A modest but legitimate single-lever attribution test on the archive's best family, with a sound secondary motivation (industry demeaning dissolves the zero-R&D mass point instead of stacking imputed firms at the global bottom), though it remains an ablation of CashCheapWithKnowledgeFloor rather than a new mechanism.

Testing conjunctive versus additive combination form is a real and unexplored design question, but the MIN operator interacts badly with the large tie mass in IND_RANK(TS_MIN(xrd/at,5)) for non-reporting firms, so a substantial fraction of firms will be capped at an identical tie value and the short leg's composition may be close to arbitrary — a diagnostic to check before interpreting any result.

Internally consistent and correctly sign-flipped off the archived negative result, but TS_RANK of a firm's own enterprise-value-to-capital ratio over five years is largely a price-level-relative-to-own-history variable, so the construct is close to the published 52-week-high/long-horizon momentum effect and the composite reduces to the well-known value-plus-momentum blend rather than an intangible-accounting mechanism.

The difference between the rank of (ceq+R&D stock)/ME and the rank of ceq/ME is essentially a monotone transform of R&D capital scaled by market equity, making this a rediscovery of the well-documented R&D-to-market-value anomaly (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis) dressed as a reclassification wedge.

The 2x2 attribution framing is appealing, but cumulative R&D share of augmented capital is cross-sectionally near-collinear with the five-year R&D-intensity floor already used in CashCheapWithKnowledgeFloor, so this is likely a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived winner and, standalone, the R&D-intensity leg is itself a known anomaly.

This is essentially an ensemble of two existing archive winners built from the same underlying `xrd` series, so the stated premise that their measurement errors are "partly independent" is unsupported — the level floor and the annual ramp are mechanically linked — and the likely outcome is an interpolation between two known alphas rather than new information.

The mechanical argument (intan inflates the ceq numerator, so the padding contaminates the ratio itself rather than merely correlating with it) is sound and makes this a legitimate grid-fill, but it substantially overlaps OrganicIntangibleValueTilt (same two ingredients, multiplicative rather than rank-difference form) which already failed at t=-1.23, so expected incremental value is modest.

`SUB(x, IND_ADJ(x))` cleanly isolates the between-industry component and converts the gen-3 demeaning result into a direct attribution test, which is genuinely diagnostic; the main caveat is that the commitment leg then varies only across a few dozen industries, so the FMB t-stat will be inflated by within-industry residual correlation and should be read with that discount.

The intangible-versus-tangible investment mix is a genuinely new channel and the industry-rank scaling of both halves is the right construction, but the `GROWTH(at,1)` half is the published asset-growth anomaly (partly absorbed by CMA in the FF5 alpha) and the reasoning misattributes a "magnitude flaw" to an earlier composition signal that actually worked (t=2.92), so the motivating diagnosis is shaky.

Deleting one `COALESCE(xad, 0)` term from an existing archive signal is the definition of a cosmetic variant, and since missing xad is already zero-filled the term cannot be contributing an "advertising-reporter tilt" in the way claimed — the coverage is identical (0.140), so the stated attribution problem is largely imaginary.

This ablation targets a structural assumption shared by nearly every archive winner — that R&D must enter both the value leg and the intangible leg — which makes it more informative than a typical single-term variant, though it reduces to plain B/M plus R&D-intensity, a pairing close to the published R&D-intensity-within-value literature, so a positive result would be hard to claim as novel.

The disjoint-population argument for pairing the R&D floor with the margin floor is economically coherent and not yet in the archive, but the nested SUMRANK mechanically halves the weight on each intangible leg while doubling the value leg's weight, so a result between the two parent signals (4.7% and 3.6%) is the most likely outcome and the test is closer to a weighted blend of two known winners than a new mechanism.

This identifies a genuine internal inconsistency in the archive's best family — EBITDA is charged for the very R&D the commitment floor rewards, whereas gross profit sits above it — and fixes it with the one value numerator not yet tested against the floor, so it is a substantive rather than cosmetic permutation despite GP/EV itself being a familiar value metric.

Deflating intan by gross profit creates a denominator that crosses and approaches zero, so firms with small or negative gross profit receive extreme or sign-flipped "productivity" ranks — negative-gross-profit distress cases score as highly productive and get rewarded in the long leg — which contradicts the stated hypothesis and makes the signal a noise-driven variant of the already-tested intan/at penalty.

Testing margin invariance versus margin floor is a legitimate and interpretable design contrast on a channel that just worked, and the argument that gross margin has no zero-imputation mass point is correct, though five annual observations make VOL a very noisy moat proxy and low margin volatility overlaps heavily with generic earnings-stability/quality tilts.

The second leg is sales-to-tangible-assets, i.e. asset turnover, which is both a published DuPont-decomposition predictor and mechanically close to the already-tested knowledge-productivity leg (sale over tangible-plus-knowledge capital, which produced ~0% alpha), and pairing it with GP/EV partly re-expresses gross-profitability rather than introducing a new economic channel.

Because GROWTH of a five-year R&D sum is a slow, low-variance series while csho growth is spiky, the second leg will be dominated by net share issuance, making this largely a rediscovery of the well-documented share-issuance anomaly combined with value rather than a test of intangible accrual to existing shareholders.

A well-motivated consolidation of two independently validated legs (GP/EV value metric and the dual unrecorded-capital floors), though the reviewer should note that gross profit now enters both legs (GP/EV numerator and the gross-margin floor), so part of any gain may be mechanical overlap rather than two independent channels.

The stated justification is internally wrong — nesting SUMRANKs re-ranks the inner composite, so the four channels do not carry exact quarter weights — and beyond that this is a kitchen-sink aggregation of already-tested legs whose outcome will be hard to attribute to any specific economic mechanism.

A clean single-lever diagnostic on the archive's strongest signal that directly tests whether the newly found margin-moat channel is firm-specific mispricing or an industry cost-structure tilt, with a defensible prior for why the answer may differ from the R&D-floor case.

The stated mechanism is inconsistent — EBITDA is already pre-amortisation, so "pre-amortisation gross profit" gives no reason to prefer GP over the incumbent numerator — leaving this a largely cosmetic numerator swap on an already-tested rank-difference signal.

The tie-mass diagnosis for the earlier conjunction failure is credible, but the test is confounded because both the value and moat legs are built from gross profit and no SUMRANK(GP/EV, margin floor) baseline exists in the archive, so a conjunction-versus-average inference will not be clean.

Distance of current gross margin from its own five-year peak is a genuinely untested state variable in this archive that plausibly separates depreciating from intact unrecorded capital, though the bounded-at-zero mass point means the long leg is effectively selected on the value leg alone and the signal may partly proxy margin momentum rather than intangible durability.

This is essentially the published intangible-adjusted (and tangible-book) value ratio of the Eisfeldt–Kim–Papanikolaou / Peters–Taylor line of work, it is merely the already-evaluated value leg of PurgedBookValueDualFloors stripped of its screens, and as a raw unranked ratio it is non-monotonic wherever the reconstructed numerator turns negative.

A legitimate and internally consistent ablation that fills a genuinely empty cell (purged book × single floor) between two existing archive results, but it is a one-term deletion from the archive's best signal rather than new economics, so its value is diagnostic rather than exploratory.

This is a four-ingredient mechanical merge of two already-tested archive winners with arbitrary nested-SUMRANK weights and no new economic content; the "complementary measurement error" claim is untestable from the proposed construction and a win here would be uninterpretable overfitting.

A single, economically coherent lever on the archive's strongest signal — capitalizing advertising alongside R&D is the natural symmetric completion of the reconstruction — though the claim that coverage cost is nil is wrong in spirit, since xad is reported sparsely and COALESCE-to-zero makes brand capital a function of disclosure practice rather than economics, which the diagnosis should acknowledge.

Pairing the corrected book ratio with the never-before-matched allocation flow is a defensible new cell and usefully breaks the archive's dependence on TS_MIN floors, but the xrd+xad−dvc leg partially re-uses the same R&D dollars already inside the value numerator, so any gain will be hard to attribute cleanly.

The double-counting hypothesis is sharp, the expression matches it exactly, and it completes the 2x2 with the two existing dual-floor results, making this the most informative of the three ablations proposed here even though it is only a one-term change.

A legitimate and clearly motivated single-term ablation that transports the equity-side redundancy finding to the firm-level formulation, but it is a narrow perturbation of FirmLevelReproducibleCapitalValue and, given that the numerator collapses to plain tangible assets over EV, the result will mostly tell you whether the R&D add-back was doing anything rather than reveal new economics.

Decomposing the purge into goodwill versus identifiable intangibles inside the value ratio is a defensible diagnostic that the earlier rank-difference test does not settle, though the construct is close to the long-known tangible-book-to-market variant and the incremental information content is modest.

This is pure lookback-parameter tuning on both screens with no change in mechanism — precisely the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against — and any alpha difference from 5-year to 3-year minima will be indistinguishable from window-selection noise.

Broadening the commitment floor to include advertising is economically coherent and untested in the screen leg, but because COALESCE(xad,0) makes non-reporters indistinguishable from non-advertisers, the floor will still be xrd-driven for most of the cross-section and any improvement should be checked for being a disclosure artifact rather than a brand-capital effect.

Framed as a substitution test it is informative, but it is largely a recombination of two archive components (PurgedValueWithAllocationChoice plus the margin floor) and the subtraction of dvc means the screen partly reduces to a non-dividend-payer tilt, which overlaps a well-documented payout/investment anomaly and should be diagnosed as such if it works.

This is the most substantively different proposal in the batch — a realised-cash value leg that sidesteps the balance-sheet reconstruction entirely — though cash-flow-to-price is itself a classic value anomaly, oancf availability will truncate the sample and coverage must be checked, and note that OCF is reduced dollar-for-dollar by expensed R&D, which mechanically works against the R&D-floor leg in the same way that motivated the gross-profit variant.

A genuine change in economic content of the moat leg rather than a window tweak, though it sits awkwardly with the companion screen — an EBITDA-margin floor mechanically penalises the very expensed R&D/advertising that the commitment leg rewards, so the two legs may partly offset and any result will need that diagnosis.

This reverses a lesson the archive already learned and documented at generation 1 (ValueWithAssetScaledIntangibleRamp explicitly moved off sales because intangible-to-sales inflates mechanically when revenue collapses, importing distressed firms into the long leg), so it is a denominator swap back to a formulation already found inferior rather than a new mechanism.

The substituted leg is essentially Novy-Marx gross-profits-to-assets with intangibles netted out, so the signal reduces to the canonical value-plus-gross-profitability combination with a spending screen attached, and it also drops the time-series-floor construction that distinguished the archive's better moat proxies without arguing why a static level is preferable.

Internally inconsistent: book equity already nets all liabilities, so subtracting net debt again double-counts leverage rather than measuring "value accruing to equity," and it will drive the numerator negative for many levered firms, making the resulting cross-sectional ranking non-monotonic in cheapness.

Coherent and correctly motivated by two separate archive results, and the point that a cumulative stock tolerates sparse advertising disclosure better than a worst-year floor is a real advantage, but the construction is only the union of two already-tested modifications and should be judged incremental unless it clears the 8.8% alpha benchmark.

A legitimate additivity test that is explicitly aimed at the archive's alpha-versus-precision tension, but mechanically it is a one-term change to FirmLevelTangibleCapitalValue, so it is only worth the slot if the equity-versus-enterprise alpha gap is actually diagnosed (leverage/cash exposure in the denominator) rather than merely re-measured.
